input_messages.content: Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.
Oh, I see. Yes, please go ahead and send me the payment request. I’d like to get this sorted out so my phone works again.
I’ve just completed the payment for the overdue bill. What should I do next to get my phone service working again? Do I need to restart my phone or anything like that?
I restarted my phone like you said, but now I see a little airplane icon at the top of the screen. Is that normal? My phone still isn’t showing any signal. What should I do next?
Oh, I didn’t realize that! Yes, please, could you help me turn off Airplane Mode? I’m not sure how to do it myself.

Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode, but my phone still says “No Signal” at the top. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose my photos if we keep doing this?
Yes, please go ahead and check the SIM status for me. I’d appreciate your help with that—I’m not very good with these things.
It looks like my SIM card is locked with a PIN code. What should I do now? I don’t remember setting up any PIN.
Yes, I think it would be best if you could transfer me to a human agent. I’m really not comfortable dealing with PIN codes and I don’t want to make things worse. Thank you for your help so far.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
